clue.text: Contact with spirit is risky

parts.note: contact is touch
with means and, joining things together
spirit or energy is go, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Someone warns that coming into contact with a ghost, or with drink, is a dangerous business.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch-and-go situation is precarious, its outcome uncertain and perilous.

clue.text: Colour of so many pigs

definitions.meaning: the hue between red and yellow
pig is an old slang word for a segment of a citrus fruit, so the whole fruit holds a number of them

explanation.surface: A question of what shade a certain number of pigs might be.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hue, and the citrus fruit is made up of segments once called pigs.

clue.text: Hundreds of hills

parts.note: a range of English chalk hills also gives its name to the Hundreds, a nominal office MPs take in order to resign their seats

explanation.surface: A landscape crowded with a great many hills.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hundred' was an old division of an English county; taking the Chiltern Hundreds is how a British MP resigns.
explanation.definitionFit: The range northwest of London gives its name to the Hundreds, the sinecure used for leaving Parliament.

clue.text: It's very hard for the first male worker in the East

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man
a worker ant, the usual crossword worker
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Life was tough for the very first man labouring in Eden, east of everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means unbreakably hard, like the legendary stone adamant.

clue.text: What darkness does daily to river swans

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Every evening the gloom falls on a riverbank full of swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Each evening the dark grows deeper and more intense as night comes on.

clue.text: No veto on port!

parts.note: no as nothing or zero is the letter O
a veto is a ban

explanation.surface: An exclamation forbidding any ban on port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but it is the harbour town of Oban on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry and fishing port on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Friend with a curly tail looking at a king in such surroundings?

definitions.text: looking at a king in such surroundings?

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: a curly thing is twisted, so the letters of tail are twisted round

explanation.surface: A dog with a curly tail gazes at a king, as in the nursery rhyme cat who looked at one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curly' turns TAIL into TIAL. The definition plays on the saying 'a cat may look at a king': royal surroundings are grand.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace, where a king lives, is grand and splendid, and so is anything palatial.

clue.text: We'll bet for a change on the girl as ringleader

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the first words are to be altered in order

parts.note: her refers to the girl

explanation.surface: A punter decides to back the girl as leader, just to try something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges WE'LL BET into BELLWET, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the leading sheep of a flock, wearing a bell, hence a leader whom others follow.

clue.text: Herb, old boy, back today's fashion

indicators.note: back tells us the letters for old boy are written in the opposite direction

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the rage is whatever is currently all the fashion

explanation.surface: A former pupil turns out to be backing the latest trend for herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Chaff is no good when it's old

parts.note: something no good is bad
when something is old it is in age, advanced in years

explanation.surface: A farmer remarks that husks of grain become useless once they have been stored too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a verb or noun means light teasing banter, which is exactly what badinage is.

clue.text: £25 to follow the hair style

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A hairdresser charges twenty-five pounds to copy the latest cut.
explanation.walkthrough: A PONY is old British betting slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: A ponytail is a hairstyle with the hair gathered at the back of the head and hanging down.

clue.text: Do these Cambridge lectures give out-of-date advice?

definitions.meaning: the ... Lecture is an annual public lecture given at the University of Cambridge
an archaic word for counsel or advice

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks whether the university's famous lecture series offers stale advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic noun means counsel, and the same name belongs to an endowed Cambridge lecture series.

clue.text: Arbitrator in Eire's troubled fuel-plants

parts.note: a referee, or ref, is an arbitrator

indicators.note: troubled suggests the words in and Eire's are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the words in Eire's spelt out with the s, Eire being the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A mediator is called in over unrest at Irish fuel plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns IN EIRES into INERIES; Eire is the Irish name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Refineries are industrial plants that purify crude oil into fuels.

clue.text: How many sheep did not stray, say, in oral examination?

definitions.text: How many sheep did not stray
definitions.meaning: in the parable of the lost sheep the shepherd leaves the flock that stayed put to find the one that wandered
a doctor examining the chest traditionally asks the patient to say this number aloud

explanation.surface: A question about the parable of the lost sheep, and a doctor's request during a check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel shepherd had a hundred sheep and one strayed, leaving that many; doctors listening to the chest ask patients to pronounce it.

clue.text: Right documents for championship performances?

definitions.meaning: papers proving legal right to own property
feats that win a championship crown, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A question about which papers suit performances that win championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Title deeds prove ownership of property; whimsically, deeds that win a championship title.

clue.text: "With a frightful, ——, fearful frown" Ko-Ko bared his big right arm

definitions.text: "With a frightful, ——, fearful frown" Ko-Ko bared his big right arm

parts.words: "With a frightful, ——, fearful frown" Ko-Ko bared his big right arm
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing adjective comes from a song in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, sung about Ko-Ko the Lord High Executioner

explanation.surface: A line from a comic opera with one word left out, describing an executioner's menacing pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Ko-Ko is the Lord High Executioner in The Mikado; the lyric runs with three alliterating F-adjectives, and the gap needs the seven-letter one meaning wild or panic-stricken.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word describes a wild, frenzied frown, fitting the alliterating string of adjectives in the lyric.

clue.text: It's chancy to drink with a party member

parts.note: ale is a drink
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: It is risky to go for a drink with a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory describes something depending on chance or luck, as in dice games.

clue.text: Secrecy is the last resort

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a new order

explanation.surface: Keeping things hidden is presented as the final option when all else fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a noun, as in last resort, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, secret action intended to avoid notice.

clue.text: Vocal modulation alternatively shown by dunnock

parts.note: an accent is a modulation or stress of the voice
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher hears the dunnock's song vary in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The dunnock is a small brown British songbird, also called the hedge sparrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The accentor family of small birds includes the dunnock, or hedge sparrow.

clue.text: Recipient of cable to give Stanley his colours

parts.note: to cap a player is to give him his colours, admitting him to a team
Stan is short for Stanley

explanation.surface: Someone sends a telegram to award Stanley his team colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his colours' completes 'to give', since to cap is to award colours; a capstan is the drum on a ship that winds the cable in.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship a capstan is the revolving drum around which an anchor cable is wound.

clue.text: Playing the gramophone? What a struggle!

definitions.meaning: a record player depends on a stylus tracking the groove, so playing records is a stylus pastime
a bitterly fought grudge match between rivals

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to get an old record player working exclaims at the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle game is a fiercely contested grudge match; playing a gramophone literally involves a needle.

clue.text: Over-cook the fish for tea

definitions.meaning: to scorch or burn food on the surface
a fish of the trout family found in cold lakes
British slang for a cup of tea, from the Chinese word

explanation.surface: Someone has burnt the fish they were preparing for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'tea' can also mean the evening meal, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to scorch, names an Arctic fish related to trout, and is colloquial British for a cuppa.

clue.text: Following direction to make pudding

parts.note: following means after
S is South, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone follows the recipe instructions to make a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is informal British for the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage afters is the sweet course served after the main meal.

clue.text: Naomi would never be so hard-hearted

parts.note: in the Book of Ruth, Naomi's daughter-in-law refused to leave her, so Naomi was never without that companion

explanation.surface: A remark that the biblical Naomi was far too kind to be cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth swore 'whither thou goest, I will go' to Naomi, so Naomi was never left without Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ruthless shows no pity or compassion, the mark of a hard heart.

clue.text: Urges a horse in two directions

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: E and S are East and South, two compass points
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A rider spurs on a horse that keeps heading two ways at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them.

clue.text: Heart set, perhaps, on show-places

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A person sets their heart on visiting famous show-places.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatres are buildings where plays and shows are staged.

clue.text: King Edward's circle at fault

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
a circle is a ring

explanation.surface: The royal circle around King Edward is blamed for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means going astray or committing an error, so being in the wrong.

clue.text: Soprano, maybe, showing vocal strain?

parts.note: vocal music is song
strain means stress

explanation.surface: A singer at the top of her range shows signs of overworking her voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is one example of a female singer.
